claims.claim: Intersect requests 1,193,000 ADA, stated as $298,250, to support Technical Steering Committee activities for 12 months.
The budget is allocated as 256,000 ADA for WP1, 832,000 ADA for WP2, and 105,000 ADA for WP3.

The funded work includes technical expert event attendance, commissioned technical reports, support for the Parameter Committee, CIP editors, Hard Fork Working Group, and a pilot independent technical review programme.
Independent technical reviews under WP3 will use formal conflict-of-interest provisions, published recusals, and open reviewer selection against documented criteria.

The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and was advanced for on-chain submission under the approved Budget Process Framework.
The requested withdrawal does not, at the time of submission, individually or in aggregate breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713.

Independent audits and assurance for this proposal will be provided by Appold, with possible reviews including deliverable verification, control testing, spend validation, and milestone evidence assessment.

The Technical Steering Committee has not received Cardano Treasury funding within the past 24 months, while Intersect and its committees received 22,385,000 ADA through listed prior governance actions.
Intersect will administer funds through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, role thresholds, and an external Oversight Committee of six entities.
Execution of the work packages is contingent on approval of the IntersectMBO budget proposal.

summary: The document requests 1,193,000 ADA for 12 months of Intersect Technical Steering Committee support, provides work-package allocations and governance controls, references external voting, audit, smart-contract, and dashboard materials, and states dependency on the IntersectMBO budget proposal approval.
